tech.summary: AI copilots are fine for individuals. But when you're dealing with sensitive IP and complex legacy systems for an enterprise? Not so much. There is an alternative - and it's trusted by 50% of the Fortune 50. Redwood RangerAI was specifically trained for service orchestration and workload automation use cases. Enterprise workflows are part of its wiring, not a prompt. Use it to: Accelerate development and reduce risk by generating automation scripts and documentation Pass task-specific data that remains private, governed and auditable Get comprehensive, real-time visibility into workflows Produce predictive SLA monitoring and intel dashboards for optimization, compliance and automatic self-recovery Meet RangerAI

tech.title: Apple invites developers to submit iPhone Duo-ready apps to the App Store
tech.summary: Apple is now accepting submissions of iPhone Duo-optimized apps and games. Xcode 27.1 Release Candidate 1 features support for building and testing apps and games for the iPhone Duo. Developers can now submit iPhone Duo-optimized apps and games in App Store Connect. App Store product pages will display a badge to let people know apps are optimized for the iPhone Duo. Recompiling existing apps with Xcode 27.1 adds development support for iPhone Duo.

tech.title: Preview, edit, and collaborate on Markdown (.md) files natively across Drive and Docs
tech.summary: Google Docs now supports Markdown files. Google Drive now renders Markdown previews. The new features are available to all Google Workspace customers and users with personal Google accounts. They will be gradually rolled out over the next two weeks.

tech.title: Controlling the brain with light earns a physiology Nobel
tech.summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel have won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their contributions to the field of optogenetics. Optogenetics involves using light to alter the behavior of nerve cells marked by the activity of individual genes. It allows researchers to activate or shut down neurons in an otherwise intact brain. The technique has revolutionized scientists' ability to understand what different populations of nerve cells are doing.

tech.title: A New Crop of Solar Panels Is the US' Best Hope of Catching China
tech.summary: Tandem solar is a new technology that adds second and third layers of material on solar panels to convert more of the Sun's radiance into electricity. Several companies plan to start selling panels commercially soon. The panels can generate 25% more energy than current available devices. Successful adoption of the technology will allow the world to meet the rapidly rising demand for electricity with less land and roof area.

tech.title: “Accelerating AI” without AI talent is a waste of time and treasure
tech.summary: AI creates workforce risks that tech alone can't resolve. This Gartner article explains how to identify the talent risks that come along with AI ambition, and the steps you need to take to unblock adoption. For more use cases and case studies, explore the thousands of stories in Gartner's AI hub

tech.title: Ephemeral testing
tech.summary: Ephemeral testing is when you test a base application layer by building on top of it. The original work is not assessed - the software built on top of it is. It is a form of integration testing, except the software on top is thrown away when the test is complete. Instead of building the core while trying to anticipate what might be needed at the other layers, you just simulate the other layers by building them.

tech.title: Why Plain Text Is Still One of the Best Technologies We Have
tech.summary: The simplicity of plain text is a large part of why it has lasted. Plain text is part of the basic plumbing of computing. There is an enormous collection of tools that know how to work with plain text, and plain text gives users more choice. Text ages surprisingly well, and it is easy to own. It is portable, inspectable, searchable, scriptable, easy to back up, and remarkably resistant to obsolescence.

tech.title: Apple and a Hacker's Future
tech.summary: CVE-2026-65400 is a high-severity macOS vulnerability that allows attackers to execute malicious code. Apple released a patch for the vulnerability last week for macOS Tahoe, Sequoia, and Sonoma. The vulnerability stems from a bug in the macOS screen sharing capability. In all observed cases, root had been accessed on the affected system and a Monero crypto miner had been placed.

tech.title: The Future of Mathematics
tech.summary: The field of mathematics is changing, but mathematics is still as important today as it ever was. Mathematics remains a core capacity for human reasoning and deliberation. Future historians will likely see this time as the start of a new era for mathematics. We are at a new frontier where communal norms, values, and expectations are beginning to break down, and the community needs to figure out what should replace them.

tech.title: The Flying Car Company Soaring Toward Wall Street
tech.summary: After nearly a decade of R&D, Doroni unveiled a showroom model of its H1-X flying car. Morgan Stanley projects a $9T market by 2050. First deliveries are targeted for 2028. Invest at $3.30/share before 10/23

tech.title: Inference Is the Most Important Market in Software
tech.summary: AI inference is set to surpass the database market to become the most important market in software.

tech.title: How Personal Agents Get Paid
tech.summary: A look at how money paid to aggregators can flow to personal agents.

tech.title: Writing blog posts while walking the dog
tech.summary: Thoughts on AI's effects on writing.

tech.title: Biosecurity, AI, and the Culture War
tech.summary: The industry's lack of consensus on what AI progress looks like is distracting it from doing practical things.

tech.title: This Is the Fitbit Edge, Google's Next Fitness Tracker
tech.summary: The Fitbit Edge will support notifications and limited apps like Google Maps, YouTube Music, and Find My Phone.

tech.title: What the AI boom is doing for Americans
tech.summary: AI is sustaining the macroeconomy in a time of huge amounts of policy uncertainty.

ai.title: Frontier intelligence. Half the bill.
ai.summary: AI coding spend is growing fast. But teams shouldn't have to choose between giving developers access to frontier intelligence and keeping token costs under control. Fireworks Nexus gives developers access to frontier open models in the harnesses they already use. With FireRouter, each request is scored and routed to the optimal model for the task, while difficult tasks can pass through to your closed provider. Set up in minutes. Keep your existing workflow. Get more control over your AI spend. 👉 Explore Fireworks Nexus

ai.title: OpenAI to Add Text Watermarks
ai.summary: OpenAI said it would add invisible text watermarks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex outputs in the EU to meet AI Act transparency requirements. Its textGrain method subtly alters word selection so generated text can be detected, though editing, translation, and short passages can weaken detection.

ai.title: Instinct in group chats
ai.summary: Instinct now lets early-access users add a shared agent to group chats for planning trips, tickets, carpools, and events. Personal Instincts enforce permissions, keep account access separate, and pause sharing when new members join.

ai.title: OpenAI in $30 Billion Round Talks With UAE Funds, BlackRock
ai.summary: OpenAI is in talks with multiple investment funds from the United Arab Emirates to help anchor a $30 billion round of financing. The UAE funds have discussed forming a syndicate to invest as much as $10 billion in the round. The University of California's endowment fund, BlackRock, Thrive Capital, and Andreessen Horowitz may also participate in the round alongside that syndicate. The fundraise is ongoing, and the details could change.

ai.title: How Devin's Memory and Dreaming Work
ai.summary: Devin's new Memory system carries preferences, corrections, and project learnings across sessions, while Dreaming periodically reorganizes and connects that information. The process deduplicates memories, links them to past sessions and artifacts, and can derive new knowledge from accumulated work.

ai.title: How to Build an AI-Native Software Factory
ai.summary: A practical look at the infrastructure companies need around coding agents once usage scales beyond individual developers. Using Uber's software factory as the main case study, it covers cloud execution, model gateways, agent identity, testing, migrations, code review, and measuring economics such as cost per merged pull request.

ai.title: OpenAI's B2B Marketplace: The Hyperscaler Of AI Apps
ai.summary: The OpenAI B2B marketplace opened on September 29 with 32 partners. OpenAI wants to position itself as the platform that the wider AI ecosystem is built on and relies on for distribution. This will consolidate AI sprawl and make it easier for customers to budget. If the marketplace gains traction, we may see an evolution similar to the cloud ecosystem where labs and AI apps co-sell, apps get charged a listing fee, and buyers receive one invoice for their spend.

ai.title: Zero Trust must extend to cover AI agents
ai.summary: AI agents act autonomously at speed and scale that challenges security frameworks. Zero Trust is insufficient to control or contain AI agents as it's currently conceived. “From Zero Trust to Agent Trust,” from Teleport , explains how to extend from Zero Trust to new Agentic Trust Principles. Read the paper →

ai.title: Framefields
ai.summary: Framefields is an npm package built for coding agents. It enables agents to create Photoshop-inspired compositing and VFX, After Effects-style motion, typography, and keyframing, and Blender-style 3D scenes, cameras, and models. The agent writes a TypeScript composition, checks frames, and renders an MP4. Framefields renders directly on GPU hardware in Node.js and modern WebGPU browsers.

ai.title: Announcing d1 with vision
ai.summary: d1, a decision model from Liquid AI, now supports images, text, or both as inputs. The model costs 19x to 200x less than GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 and answers significantly faster on every task. It outputs probabilities for yes/no, choice, or score questions in one forward pass without generating tokens. Text decisions are made in 200 to 300 milliseconds.

ai.title: Reflection Introduces Beam Model
ai.summary: Beam is a 501B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 23B active parameters trained for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. The model used 23.8T pretraining tokens and more than 100M reinforcement-learning rollouts, with open weights and developer artifacts planned for release later in October.

ai.title: OpenAI Expands Ads in ChatGPT
ai.summary: OpenAI introduced a new visual ad format in ChatGPT alongside expanded measurement tools, partnerships, and brand-suitability work. The company positioned advertising as a way to support broader access to ChatGPT while giving businesses another channel to reach users during product discovery and decision-making.

ai.title: Two Room-Temperature Antiferromagnetic Semiconductor Candidates
ai.summary: Ferromagnets' atomic magnets all point the same way, adding their magnetic effects. Antiferromagnets have neighboring atomic magnets that point opposite ways and exactly cancel out magnetically. There is an intense drive in computer memory research to create materials in between these two extremes. This post details how a team of AI agents designed a candidate magnet for next-generation computer memory that has zero net magnetism yet still sorts electrons by spin.

ai.title: Power your AI agents with a real-time web search API
ai.summary: Agents are smarter when they can search the web. Give any AI agent access to live search engine data in JSON or Markdown format with SerpApi. Try it now.

ai.title: Asset Light Software
ai.summary: Software businesses are shifting from fixed costs toward variable, consumption-based costs as AI automates junior work and commoditizes software creation.

ai.title: Etched fields funding offers at $40B+ valuation, sources say
ai.summary: While it seems like a fast timetable to raise another mega round (Etched raised $700 million at a $21 billion valuation a couple of months ago), the company is pursuing a particularly expensive segment of the AI industry: building full AI hardware systems powered by proprietary chips.

ai.title: 10 Takeaways from Tibo Sottiaux
ai.summary: OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux expects agents to take most internet actions, model pickers to disappear, and models to improve roughly 10x within a year.

ai.title: Self-Modeling Interventions Modulate Emergent Misalignment
ai.summary: Interventions on AI models' self-models, through self-recognition and self-report, can modulate and mitigate Emergent Misalignment.

ai.title: Living Models pairs Gemma 4 with BOTANIC-1 to help decode plant DNA
ai.summary: Living Models pairs Gemma 4 with BOTANIC-1, compressing years of crop genetics into hours.

ai.title: Nvidia's $20 billion Groq deal faces lawsuit alleging startup's stockholders were shortchanged
ai.summary: The deal was allegedly made without the stockholder vote that Delaware law requires and without any process designed to test or maximize the value of what Nvidia bought.

ai.title: North 2: Enterprise AI Without Compromises
ai.summary: Cohere's North 2 platform eliminates trade-offs in security, intelligence, cost, and control for enterprises adopting agentic AI.

webdev.title: Build serverless microservices on AWS
webdev.summary: Learn how to build serverless microservices that react to database events in real time. This AWS tutorial walks through building an event-driven system by connecting Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and MongoDB Atlas on AWS Marketplace . You'll learn how to detect database changes, trigger automated workflows, and deploy scalable services without managing infrastructure. Whether you're launching new features or modernizing legacy systems, get step-by-step guidance to move faster while cutting integration overhead. Read the step-by-step tutorial.

webdev.title: Build an agent loop a small model can finish
webdev.summary: A reliable agent loop depends less on model size than on a trustworthy check that turns progress into a score or pass condition. In two visual tasks, small models improved dramatically when they received repeatable feedback across varied examples and holdout cases, while weak checks encouraged overfitting or shortcuts.

webdev.title: How we built the fastest, cheapest browser agent with Jev
webdev.summary: IronBee Express uses Jev as a fast classifier for bounded browser decisions, calling an LLM only for writing, recovery, or failure explanations. Explored runs cost about $0.0042 for 20 actions, recordings can replay with no step decisions, and narrow verification questions helped a 130-run replay test reach 130 correct outcomes.

webdev.title: Chat is AI's command line
webdev.summary: Chat is useful for rough direction, but it becomes awkward when people need to make precise edits or understand the state of ongoing work. The piece argues for AI interfaces built around direct manipulation, visible state, and reversible experimentation, much like spreadsheets and graphical desktops expanded computing beyond the command line.

webdev.title: Ephemeral testing
webdev.summary: Ephemeral testing evaluates a software component by asking an AI agent to build disposable applications or layers on top of it, then judging how well those downstream projects work. Repeating the exercise with different agents and tasks can expose hidden state, unstable invariants, surprising defaults, and weak documentation.

webdev.title: Docusign API or MCP? How to choose the right standard for your agreement data
webdev.summary: Keyword-based queries don't work for large agreement repositories because contract language is often inconsistent. This guide explains how the Docusign Agreement Manager API and MCP Server use AI to surface relevant insights, and how to choose the right approach for your task. Start building with a free developer account

webdev.title: TanStack Charts 1.0
webdev.summary: TanStack Charts 1.0 offers a composable, type-safe charting system built from marks, scales, axes, and interactions instead of rigid chart types. It supports custom marks and renderers, optional SVG or Canvas output, modular animation and scale packages, and a stable API intended to evolve without forcing applications to rebuild their visualizations.

webdev.title: Introducing Beam: Reflection's 501B open-weight model
webdev.summary: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501 billion total parameters and 23 billion active parameters aimed at coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Reflection trained it on 23.8 trillion tokens and more than 100 million reinforcement learning rollouts, with Apache 2.0 weights and developer artifacts planned for release later this month.

webdev.title: How Booking.com cut Node.js costs by 38% with Watt
webdev.summary: Booking.com moved a major Node.js rendering service from pm2 clustering to Watt worker threads, cutting compute costs by 38% with 30% fewer pods, 20% less memory per pod, and up to 10% lower tail latency. The migration required no service code changes, and production tests showed 40% to 50% more throughput within the same latency target.

webdev.title: Worth building
webdev.summary: Cheaper software development makes small tools worthwhile even when they solve one person's annoyance and never become a business. As more people can ship, the story behind a project and the choices that shaped it become increasingly important reasons for others to care.

webdev.title: An Embeddable Office Editor With 900+ API Methods for AI Apps & Agents
webdev.summary: Add AI document creation and editing to your app. Give your agents object-level APIs for DOCX, XLSX and PPTX, and users an embedded editor. Try the playground

webdev.title: CSS does your tooltip positioning now
webdev.summary: CSS anchor positioning, position fallbacks, popovers, and anchor-size() can now handle responsive tooltip and dropdown placement with little or no JavaScript, though component-scoped anchor names and accessible DOM order still matter.

webdev.title: Introducing Web Search API
webdev.summary: Cloudflare's beta Web Search API lets agents search through Ceramic.ai, Exa, or Linkup via AI Gateway with Zero Data Retention, gateway logging, and provider list pricing without added markup.

webdev.title: The performance cost of RwLock in a read-heavy workload
webdev.summary: A Rust benchmark found that replacing 16,384 per-item RwLock acquisitions with one Crossbeam epoch guard and atomic pointer loads raised read throughput from 15.93k to 229.07k operations per second, while a simple lock still worked well around an infrequently changed collection.

webdev.title: Two Room-Temperature Antiferromagnetic Semiconductor Candidates
webdev.summary: AI agents identified two candidate room-temperature Luttinger-compensated semiconductors for spintronic memory, but one may be difficult to synthesize, and the other still needs direct measurement of its band gap and spin sorting.

infosec.title: When AI agents make the wrong call, few can reconstruct what happened
infosec.summary: That's because agents break tools built for humans. To govern them, you need to get clarity about the 5 sources of enterprise AI risk. Airia's State of Enterprise AI Risk report explains how: Ungoverned AI is the risk that compounds every other one Model risk does not end at deployment Vendor-embedded agents can access enterprise systems without appearing in your inventory Most organizations cannot say who approved an agent's decision, or who was responsible for the policy behind it Download your report

infosec.title: Bouncy Castle CVE-2026-71885 Harvested the Credential Binding That Authenticates Agent-to-Agent Channels
infosec.summary: A critical vulnerability in Bouncy Castle for Java versions before 1.86 lets attackers spoof legitimate participants and decrypt messages within Messaging Layer Security groups. Improper certificate validation in the protocol implementation lets threat actors bypass core security objectives by presenting arbitrary credentials. Developers must upgrade to version 1.86 to enforce cryptographic binding between end-entity certificates and LeafNode signature keys.

infosec.title: New Dell System Update flaw lets hackers gain root privileges
infosec.summary: A critical path traversal flaw in Dell System Update (CVE-2026-86360) allowed unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code as root on PowerEdge servers using the DSU deployment tool. Dell's advisory also addressed four other high-severity DSU vulnerabilities: two that enable remote code execution (CVE-2026-63697 and CVE-2026-71168) and two that enable privilege escalation (CVE-2026-86361 and CVE-2026-86362). None have been reported as exploited so far. Admins should upgrade to DSU 2.3.0.0 or later.

infosec.title: Roundcube Webmail SQL Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-48842 Under Active Exploitation
infosec.summary: Unauthenticated attackers are actively exploiting a pre-authentication SQL injection vulnerability in Roundcube Webmail versions 1.6.0 through 1.6.15 and 1.7.0 to execute arbitrary database commands and access sensitive data. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-48842, resides in the built-in virtuser_query plugin. Administrators must immediately update to versions 1.6.16 or 1.7.1, or disable the vulnerable plugin.

infosec.title: Open Build Service, one year later: command execution through Mercurial argument injection
infosec.summary: Fenrisk found CVE-2026-56004 in Open Build Service's obs_scm Mercurial backend. An attacker-controlled _service revision beginning with --config could set a pre-update hook and run shell commands on the service server. A space in the value bypassed Python argparse handling of dash-prefixed arguments. Exploitation required Mercurial, a reachable HTTP(S) repository, and a successful clone. Fenrisk confirmed build.opensuse.org was vulnerable. openSUSE patched the flaw on July 2 by adding -- before the revision and recommending rejection of dash-prefixed revisions.

infosec.title: A peek into Reddit's anti-spam internals
infosec.summary: A 2021 Reddit glitch exposed internal removal reasons in Relay notifications. Screenshots reveal domain blocks, account bans, shadowbans, Spamurai rules, and URL inspection. Spamurai logged account age, karma, reports, ISP, email domain, browser details, language headers, TLS fingerprints, and referrers. This reproduced a Perspective API score and showed that appending two letters changed a spam score from 86% to 1%. Reddit also followed redirected URLs, scanned page content, and matched a Google Analytics ID tied to a spam ring.

infosec.title: Your car is a smartphone on wheels. Here's who's listening
infosec.summary: Northeastern researchers and Consumer Reports captured Wi-Fi traffic from 21 vehicles through a Raspberry Pi access point, decrypted 30 companion iOS apps with mitmproxy, and found that 19 vehicles contacted at least one third party, including ad and tracking domains. Seven apps sent VINs, emails, phone numbers, or precise location to trackers, and GM's four apps shared VINs with ten companies, including Meta, Google, and Acxiom. Pairing a companion app roughly doubled a vehicle's tracker exposure on average, and of 17 manufacturers contacted, most shifted responsibility to owners. One notable exception: Honda improved its data collection practices to avoid sending precise geolocation information to a third party involved in user tracking.

infosec.title: Coi
infosec.summary: Coi protects host credentials and files by isolating AI coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex inside Linux system containers during autonomous sessions. The open-source tool uses Incus, a lightweight LXD fork, to grant root access, systemd, and native Docker, alongside kernel-level threat detection that automatically pauses or kills compromised containers.

infosec.title: Guardana
infosec.summary: Guardana is an open-source AI security verification tool for security and platform engineers. It checks code and model artifacts, live AI systems, and recorded runs. It reports what it found, what it could not verify, and what it could not check. It verifies outside the request path. Guardana is not an inline guardrail, a general SAST or CVE scanner, or a compliance certification.

infosec.title: doxx.net (Product Launch)
infosec.summary: doxx.net has launched ADN, a private network with peer-to-peer messaging, file transfers, custom domains, and DNS threat blocking. It blocks malicious destinations before connections and uses proof-of-work accounts without usernames, passwords, or personal data.

infosec.title: Apple and a Hacker's Future
infosec.summary: A Claude Code agent flagged a root-level Monero miner on Ben Thompson's always-on Mac Mini after attackers exploited CVE-2026-65400, a macOS screen sharing flaw, through an internet-exposed port 5900. Thompson kept screen sharing on because headless Macs need someone to click GUI-only TCC prompts, and he found that the automatic security updates setting did not cover the point release carrying the fix. He argues that Apple's planned Full Disk Access restrictions push macOS further toward a managed device, at odds with agent-driven computing.

infosec.title: Senate Passes Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Healthcare Cybersecurity
infosec.summary: The Senate passed the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resilience Act by unanimous consent. The bill moves to the House. It funds prevention, incident response, and security training. It directs HHS and CISA coordination, names ASPR as sector risk manager, and requires an HHS incident-response plan.

infosec.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say
infosec.summary: Jordanian authorities detained alleged ShinyHunters member Saif al-Din Khader, known as Rey. Two sources said he is helping the FBI identify other members through his devices and correspondence with a sample of stolen FBI data containing employee identities, job details, and medical and psychiatric records. The group's dark-web site disappeared after another alleged member was detained in the Netherlands.

infosec.title: Linux 7.4 To Land New BTB CTX Isolation Feature Of AMD Zen 6
infosec.summary: Linux 7.4 will support AMD Zen 6's BTB CTX Isolation, which separates user/kernel and guest/host branch predictor contexts.

infosec.title: Google froze its open source bug bounty program due to a ‘significant rise' in AI submissions
infosec.summary: Google paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program on October 1 after automated reports flooded maintainers and engineers.

infosec.title: Data breach hits Denmark's population register, affecting 8.8 million
infosec.summary: Names, addresses, and CPR numbers for about 8.8 million people were exposed after attackers accessed Denmark's Central Population Register, reportedly using a Danish company's legitimate login credentials.

product.title: The behavioral signals you trust stopped meaning what you think
product.summary: Your dashboard says this was a good year: error clicks down, post-error exits down. But in the same sessions, rage clicks rose 77% and suspicious activity rose roughly 10x. Fullstory's 2026 Digital Benchmark Report tracked 18.7 billion sessions across 2,600+ companies to find out which metrics actually mean what teams think they mean. See how your own numbers stack up against 11 industry benchmarks Find out if your metrics are actually improving, or just look like they are Benchmark Your Data

product.title: The Future of Knowledge Inside the Enterprise
product.summary: Enterprise knowledge management creates business value by connecting organizational experience to AI agents acting under human accountability. Establishing a context layer over existing systems extends expertise, improves efficiency, enhances verification, and strengthens continuity through a structured operating model.

product.title: Building is cheap. Owning it is not
product.summary: While modern tools and AI make building software products cheaper, the cost of ownership and making strategic choices remains high. Dedicated PMs add value by focusing on business viability, ranking roadmap bets, tracking clear predictions, and acting as communication bridges and quality gatekeepers for their teams.

product.title: Before You Build, Ask Yourself: Who is Your Bullseye Customer?
product.summary: Early-stage product teams should define a one-sentence Bullseye Customer hypothesis before building. Specifying the target customer, trigger, and outcome surfaces hidden team disagreements and improves user research.

product.title: Product ethics in the age of AI (13 minute podcast)
product.summary: Product ethics in the age of artificial intelligence must become a core success factor alongside desirability, feasibility, and viability, rather than remaining an afterthought. This podcast episode explains how to integrate ethical considerations into the innovation process, factor them into strategy updates, and measure a product's ethical impact.

product.title: A Manifesto on How a Modern Research Team Should Work
product.summary: Modern UX research teams fail when researchers work in isolation. To fix this, teams should adopt shared goals, conduct weekly peer critiques, maintain a central user research record, and enforce clear rules for study requests.

product.title: A New Kind of AI Model: Jev and Quick Wins for PMs
product.summary: TypeSafe AI's Jev is a decision model that outputs probabilities rather than text. Operating at low cost and high speed, it supports binary questions, multiple-choice selections, and scoring.

product.title: The fake double diamond is dead. The real double diamond is immortal
product.summary: The product development dichotomy between upfront definition and continuous iteration is a false choice. True innovation requires balancing upfront discovery with ongoing observation within a cohesive system. Relying on artificial shortcuts or AI-driven alignment ultimately degrades software quality and prevents teams from solving complex problems.

product.title: Users don't hate change. They hate you
product.summary: Users do not inherently hate change - they resent updates that destroy their familiarity and control without clear benefit. Citing psychological research on loss aversion, the article explains that users weigh losses in comfort far more than potential gains, criticizing tech companies for forcing redesigns without explaining their value.

product.title: What I learned getting acquired by Google
product.summary: A co-founder of Socratic reflects on their startup's acquisition by Google, detailing the challenges of rebuilding their product on Google's stack while navigating reorgs, reviews, and process debt.

product.title: 10 things OpenAI's Tibo thinks builders are underestimating about AI
product.summary: Tibo Sottiaux highlights upcoming shifts in AI, emphasizing that product teams must build for faster, cheaper, and more capable models while focusing on user understanding and taste.

design.title: The Brisbane 2032 Olympics logo is hiding a triple design in plain sight
design.summary: The Brisbane 2032 Olympic emblem combines three ideas in a single vivid form: an Olympic flame, the crest of Australia's native cockatoo, and the shape of Queensland. Its pink-and-red form gives the identity an energetic, playful character intended to feel distinctly connected to the host region. The identity was accidentally revealed early through an explainer uploaded to Brisbane 2032's YouTube channel.

design.title: John Ternus is taking a more ‘hands-on' role in Apple's design teams as CEO
design.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus has reportedly become deeply involved with the company's industrial design and human interface teams, working in the design studio several times a week and sometimes visiting multiple times per day. Rather than appointing a new chief design officer, Apple has Molly Anderson leading industrial design and Steve Lemay leading human interface design, with Ternus acting as the overarching decision-maker. Apple is also rebuilding teams depleted by departures to companies including Meta and OpenAI through internal promotions and external hires.

design.title: OpenAI launches visual ads that appear alongside image generation results
design.summary: OpenAI is adding visual display ads alongside images generated in ChatGPT, starting later this month in the US with a small group of advertisers. The ads will be clearly labeled and, according to OpenAI, will not influence ChatGPT's answers. The company is also expanding ad measurement partnerships and developing brand suitability evaluations as it builds an ad-supported business for users on free and low-cost plans.

design.title: Training AI to Paint with Code
design.summary: A language model was trained with reinforcement learning to create watercolor images by writing editable p5.brush JavaScript rather than generating fixed image files, giving people direct control over the resulting artifact. Early training exposed problems with overly complex reward systems, while switching from absolute scores to pairwise comparisons against a hand-rated reference pool produced better images with dramatically shorter code. The experiment shows that applying reinforcement learning to creative work is fundamentally a design problem: subjective qualities like taste need carefully constructed reward structures that provide direction without forcing the model toward a single aesthetic.

design.title: 10 Uncomfortable UX Lessons from Real Design Mistakes
design.summary: Ten uncomfortable lessons from real design mistakes offer a way to make better design choices before running more UX tests. Minimalism failed on an ERP shipment form, and a standard landing page beat an artistic, scroll-snapping one in an A/B test. Other lessons favor preventing errors over recovering from them, and giving users an opt-out instead of forcing AI into manual workflows.

design.title: What Are the Principles of Prototyping?
design.summary: A prototype is a way to learn something before making a bigger commitment, in any form, from an email or text message to an event. Nine principles, refined by 124 people at Services Week 2026, hold that a prototype answers a question, is tested with future users, and can be archived. The tools have changed, with AI-assisted ones now in the mix, but the purpose and principles of prototyping have not.

design.title: Inspect Any Page with No Site Access Requested
design.summary: A free, open-source browser extension that inspects layout, styles, color, type, and assets on any page.

design.title: Turning Product Managers and Product Designers into Product Builders
design.summary: AutonomyAI lets PMs and designers create production code changes for engineering approval, so engineers stay focused on what only they can build.

design.title: RuneIcons - Beautiful Icons for Your Next Project
design.summary: Rune Icons is a free, open-source library of more than 900 hand-drawn icons available in outline, duotone, fill, pixel, and glass styles, with browser-based controls for editing paths, stroke, size, color, and motion before copying them as SVG or JSX.

design.title: Workflow Lab: From Design System to Campaign in Figma Weave
design.summary: A product designer at a fictional museum uses Figma Weave to turn the museum's design system into campaign collateral for a new exhibition. Image Describer nodes read existing designs and color families, and the Gen Effect node gives every image a shared look through color grading and hazy edges. The Figma node stays connected, so design-system updates flow downstream, and the node graph can be reused for future shows or published as a Weave tool.

design.title: Design is a Nice-to-Have
design.summary: Design feels like a nice-to-have again, according to a designer who now builds software himself and finds news about design craft and tools flat. Once programming became trivial, design lost the spotlight it briefly held when SaaS commoditized software and distribution was the hardest part. Craft still matters, but a "good enough" UX suffices, since usefulness to the market was always what mattered most.

design.title: Brand Identity: Koto's Stack Overflow Rebrand
design.summary: Koto has repositioned Stack Overflow as a source of human-validated knowledge in an AI-first world, consolidating its portfolio and building the identity around the concept “Always in Build.” A simplified stack-shaped logo expands into a generative visual language of geometry that continuously reformats and rebuilds, supported by an expanded orange-led palette and the custom Stack Sans typeface with distinctive notched letterforms. A custom generative tool lets Stack Overflow's team produce new compositions at scale, while the system stays restrained inside the product and becomes more expressive across campaigns and the Developer Survey.

design.title: Seven Reasons Non-Artists Need a Drawing Pad on Their Desk
design.summary: Non-artists can put the handmade Japanese Drawing Pad to seven uses, from brain-dumping to-do lists and mind-mapping to journaling and doodling away stress.

design.title: Télio Péron Blends Photoreal Detail with Supernatural Imagination to Create 3D Environments That Never Fully Explain Themselves
design.summary: French 3D artist Télio Péron grounds slightly impossible elements, from glowing artifacts to folklore creatures, in photoreal forests, moss, and weathered wood.

marketing.title: PSA: Your brand already has an AI fingerprint
marketing.summary: You don't have to guess how AI interprets your brand. Markup AI's Free Brand Profile analyzes your publicly available content to articulate your voice, distinctive writing patterns, target personas, and preferred terminology. It then hands you a standard you can use to review content wherever you're already working. If you don't like what you see, you know what to change . Simply input your email and your company domain to get AI's view. No strings attached. Get your Free Brand Profile

marketing.title: Experiential Marketing Trend: Brand Gazettes
marketing.summary: Brand gazettes are becoming a way for brands to extend physical events into tangible content experiences. Publications are designed specifically for an activation and give attendees something to read and keep after the event. Grey Goose used its Gazette to tell stories about the brand's French heritage while Disney recreated the fictional Runway magazine from The Devil Wears Prada 2 as a real 90-page issue. QR codes and other interactive elements can also connect print content to digital experiences.

marketing.title: Cash-Strapped Americans Tap Home Equity and AI to Keep Spending
marketing.summary: Consumers are maintaining spending despite higher prices by finding ways to offset rising costs. Grocery prices are up 32% since 2020, yet spending on cars, clothing, and restaurants still increased in August. Some consumers are using credit or drawing from savings while others are cutting costs elsewhere. AI is also becoming a budgeting tool, with one consumer using ChatGPT to compare grocery prices and save about $100 a month.

marketing.title: You automated your build. Your growth is still manual
marketing.summary: Growth compounds when each marketing activity creates inputs for the next one. The author focuses on 3 growth loops: app installs can improve store visibility, content can inform the next post, and product usage can generate reviews and user content. The content loop is often the slowest because it requires the most manual work, yet it can have significant results. Find the slowest step in each loop and remove unnecessary manual handoffs so each cycle happens faster.

marketing.title: We Vibe Coded Our Own Calendly. Our AI Agent Pushed Us To Do It, and It Was Right
marketing.summary: A 3-person team built its own scheduling tool in 20 mins after its AI agent identified a limitation with Calendly. The custom booker connects scheduling to Salesforce and prospect data, showing each prospect a personalized prospectus and routing them to the right salesperson based on account ownership. The team could have integrated Calendly, but the agent determined that most of the custom logic would still need to be built. The default remains buying software, with custom builds reserved for narrow workflows where proprietary data creates an advantage.

marketing.title: Stop asking your visitors to hunt for info. Let them talk to your website instead
marketing.summary: Turn your website from pages people browse into conversations that convert. CrafterQ learns from your content and gives every visitor an AI agent that answers questions, recommends next steps, and captures leads — helping turn website traffic into customers. See how it works.

marketing.title: Prediction: the next massive Google update is around the corner
marketing.summary: Google tends to rewrite its documentation shortly before a major update, and it has just rewritten its guidance on AI content and authorship. Publishing AI text at scale without manual review now counts as little to no effort, and invented authors with AI headshots count as deception. The GEO tactics built to win AI answers, including self-ranking listicles and paid mentions, repeat old SEO spam patterns that Google has historically shut down. Cutting or consolidating scaled content before an update is often easier than recovering after one.

marketing.title: Building advertising for the way people use AI
marketing.summary: OpenAI is testing visual ads in ChatGPT that show products and services through images during image generation. The format lets advertisers demonstrate products in use and link to more information. ChatGPT Ads are also adding conversion tracking and attribution through partners including Hightouch, Tealium, LiveRamp, AppsFlyer, and Triple Whale. Testing starts in the US later this month.

marketing.title: The Economics of the Streak: Loyalty Programs and Stars
marketing.summary: Loyalty programs use loss aversion and goal gradients to make accumulated points feel like possessions worth protecting. A 100-day streak can become more motivating to preserve than the underlying habit, while being close to a reward or tier encourages extra spending. Programs also benefit from unredeemed points through breakage and collect purchase data. They can reward behaviors customers already value or drive spending and engagement mainly to avoid losing accumulated progress.

marketing.title: I shopped for soccer shoes with ChatGPT, Claude, and Muse. One got me closer to buying
marketing.summary: AI shopping assistants need to balance choice with guidance to build purchase confidence. ChatGPT won by showing 3 soccer shoe options with a recommended pick and clear comparison. Claude offered useful product details but lacked images and purchase links. Muse made shopping more engaging with interactive questions and visuals but recommended the wrong shoes. The test suggests giving shoppers a few options plus a clear recommendation can make AI-assisted purchases easier.

marketing.title: Clean up your UA tags
marketing.summary: Search Google Tag Manager for old “Universal Analytics” or “UA-” tags, pause them for a week, then remove them if nothing breaks.

marketing.title: I analyzed 1,100+ job posts with Claude Code. Here's what B2B marketers get paid
marketing.summary: B2B marketing salaries range from a $119K median for early-career roles to $300K for VP and CMO roles.

crypto.title: Get started trading the original digital asset: domain names
crypto.summary: For over 30 years, thousands of people have made a full-time income from investing in domain names. With over $1 billion of domains traded annually, domain investing is still big business. Learning which domain names to buy, and how to sell them is crucial. GoDaddy's Domain Academy is the key to helping you to invest in domain names like a pro. Join the #1 domain training platform in the world, trusted by thousands of individuals and companies. → Learn to invest in domain names

crypto.title: Strategy buys 334 BTC for $28.7 million as total holdings top 848,000 BTC
crypto.summary: Strategy bought 334 BTC for $28.7 million at an average of $85,838.80 between September 28 and October 4, bringing total holdings to 848,000 BTC, its highest ever and worth about $73 billion against a cost basis near $64 billion (average $75,440.70 per coin). The purchase was funded by $15.7 million in MSTR at-the-market stock sales and $13 million from its USD cash reserve, with $18.8 billion of MSTR still available under the program. Strategy also repurchased 1.77 million STRC preferred shares for $176.3 million last week and held $4.88 billion in its USD Reserve as of October 4, while MSTR fell 7.1% on the week to $160.01.

crypto.title: CFTC proposes new federal framework for leveraged retail crypto trading
crypto.summary: The CFTC launched a rulemaking to create a federal pathway for leveraged and margined retail crypto trading through proposed Regulation CTX and Regulation CAM, including a new "crypto asset market" category of CFTC-registered exchanges. Unlike the failed Clarity Act, the rules would not force crypto assets onto CFTC-registered platforms, since Chairman Michael Selig said the agency lacks that authority without congressional action. The move follows the Clarity Act's September failure in the Senate, with the SEC and CFTC both pushing ahead on their own rulemaking.

crypto.title: Ethereum Foundation Launches zkAPI for Private API Access
crypto.summary: The Ethereum Foundation released zkAPI, a zero-knowledge protocol that lets users access paid APIs without exposing their identity, counterparty, or consumption patterns to any intermediary. Users deposit ETH into a vault, generate a ZK proof, and receive a fixed quota of API access, with payment metadata abstracted away so no on-chain or off-chain trace links usage back to the caller. OA-chat is live with zkAPI integrated, and the design generalizes to any gated API resource beyond AI inference. Prior unlinkable inference schemes leaked payment trails - zkAPI closes that gap by separating payment metadata from identity at the protocol layer.

crypto.title: Melee Opens Permissionless Market Creation in Phase 2
crypto.summary: Melee bootstrapped 10,000+ price markets and $337.7M in volume over three weeks in Phase 1 by running 5-minute BTC, SOL, and ANSEM rounds 24/7 through its PMM (parimutuel market maker), which pools participant capital and distributes winnings proportionally without requiring external market makers or liquidity incentives. Phase 2 opens market creation to anyone via Melee templates, letting creators claim a market, share it with their audience, and collect fees, with weekly competitions awarding badges to the top markets by volume and unique trader count. The PMM architecture addresses the cold-start liquidity problem that blocks long-tail prediction markets from launching without subsidized counterparties, replacing that dependency with a self-contained pooling mechanism. Creator Score, a reputation layer rating operators by activity, and Phase 3 fully permissionless market creation are next on the roadmap.

crypto.title: SMBC Nikko Building Regulated DeFi Gateway for Japan on Uniswap
crypto.summary: SMBC Nikko and Nethermind are building the DeFi Gateway, a regulated onchain trading venue on Uniswap v4 targeting Japanese investors, with Uniswap Labs, Base, and Nyx Foundation supporting development toward a mid-2027 target. Each pool uses Uniswap v4 hooks to enforce AML/CFT checks and investor protections, embedding Japan's regulatory requirements directly into pool logic. Supported assets span stablecoins, RWAs, and other digital assets, and the pool framework is open for third-party teams to build on. SMBC Nikko and Nethermind will also develop AI-powered vaults and investor onboarding interfaces, with Uniswap Labs advising on integration and liquidity deployment.

crypto.title: Tokenization Was the Easy Part
crypto.summary: Institutional demand for tokenization centers on operational efficiency for familiar assets rather than new asset classes, with clients prioritizing faster settlement, easier venue portability, and collateral utility without forced liquidation. Traditional fund architecture fragments transactions, settlement, and ownership records across separate systems, and moving ownership records onchain consolidates those processes into a single layer. Ethereum Foundation researcher Barnabé Monnot frames this as Ethereum's opening: 100% historical uptime, fast slots and finality arriving via decoupled consensus work, and broad ZK availability replacing multisig trust assumptions together position Ethereum as the global settlement layer.

crypto.title: Fintech is Dead
crypto.summary: Fintech's founding assumptions (mobile-first, cloud-native, and API banking) have become table stakes across all financial services, driving the sector's share of global VC from 14.5% in 2021 to 12.3% in 2025, while the share of fintech capital flowing to AI companies jumped from roughly 10% to 70-80%. The successor architecture runs on two primitives: intelligence tokens and value tokens, joined by a router layer that prices AI inference in deterministic on-chain value millions of times per second. Stripe's $7B acquisition of OpenRouter and Ramp's simultaneous launch of Router.com signal that both operators concluded AI token routing is core financial infrastructure. Downstream, Revolut's PRAGMA model detected 130% more bad credit risk, Figure's tokenized HELOC marketplace cleared $2.8B in quarterly volume at 95% adjusted net-revenue growth, and Robinhood opened 100,000 MCP-enabled agent accounts.

crypto.title: Market Maturation: Crypto Liquid Thoughts, Q4 2026
crypto.summary: The July bottom is confirmed at BTC $59k and ETH $1.6k, and sorts the ensuing bull market opportunity into two buckets: protocols that ARE money (stores of value with uncapped BTC-relative upside) and protocols that MAKE money. For revenue-generating protocols, investors will apply traditional public-market filters, including revenue quality and durability, margin profiles, and institutional access, with the strongest positioning going to projects exposed to RWA and stablecoin growth, backed by founder-CEOs who survived prior bear markets. Onchain AI infrastructure plays (routers, inference, compute, and data) are framed as narrative trades, with specific skepticism around structures where value accrues to equity rather than the token, and a hard run in that category flagged as a potential cycle-top signal.

crypto.title: S&P Global launches AAA-style risk scores for DeFi lending vaults
crypto.summary: S&P Global Ratings launched a "Vault Risk Assessment" that grades on-chain lending vaults.

crypto.title: ETH staking hits an all-time high of 36% of supply
crypto.summary: 36% of all ETH is now staked, up from 29% at the start of the year, with about 8.2 million ETH (around $22 billion) staked in 2026 alone.

crypto.title: A framework for fintech ideas: turn something complex into an API
crypto.summary: The best way to find new fintech ideas is to ask how a complex product can become an API.

crypto.title: RIFT Launches as Universal Onchain Routing API
crypto.summary: RIFT launched an onchain routing API that sources best-price execution across all liquidity venues in a single call, charging zero added fees.

it.title: Schneider Electric agrees to acquire PTC for $22.6B
it.summary: Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal valuing its equity at $22.6 billion, with closing expected by Q3 2027 pending approvals. The combination would connect PTC's product design and engineering data with Schneider's operational and energy systems, providing broader context for industrial AI applications.

it.title: Reflection unveils 501B-parameter AI model Beam
it.summary: Beam is a 501-billion-parameter model that Reflection says competes with leading Chinese models while requiring substantially less compute. Access initially runs through an early-access program, with model weights, documentation, and fine-tuning tools planned for release later this month.

it.title: Huawei and Qualcomm Announce Broad Patent License Agreement
it.summary: Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multi-year, broad patent license agreement featuring cross-licenses across technology fields including 5G, compute, AI, and networking. Additionally, the agreement includes Qualcomm's purchase of certain Huawei US patents in compute, AI, and networking. The transaction is pending necessary regulatory approvals.

it.title: AI productivity needs an organizational redesign
it.summary: McKinsey argues that individual productivity gains will struggle to translate into business value unless companies redesign workflows, decision rights, and career paths around human–agent teams. Its proposed approach organizes teams around outcomes, reduces handoffs, and explicitly assigns responsibility for agent actions and the capacity automation frees up.

it.title: How Oracle gives AI agents access without handing over control
it.summary: Oracle details how it preserves employee permissions across MCP connections and limits coding and operations agents through temporary access, least privilege, and human approval for sensitive actions. The deployment offers a practical example of enforcing authorization in backend systems as assistants move from retrieving information to executing work.

it.title: Registered but not routed: what a global audit of IPv6 says about deployment
it.summary: Researchers conducted a global audit comparing IPv6 registration records from Regional Internet Registries against live BGP routing tables and the IPv6 Hitlist project. They found that while 92.5 percent of registered IPv6 netblocks appear in live routing, only 79.4 percent of the underlying address space does, revealing a large gap concentrated in unannounced legacy allocations and carrier-grade NAT deployments. Furthermore, cross-checking against the IPv6 Hitlist project identified 28.1 million genuinely distinct, confirmed-live hosts, highlighting a massive amount of unrouted and unmonitored address space worldwide.

it.title: The #1 rated password manager, now 50% off
it.summary: Protect yourself (and your family) against cybercriminals without having to remember complex passwords. Keeper securely stores unique login credentials for all your accounts, encrypted so only you can access them. Eliminate weak passwords, streamline access control, and reduce breach risk across your personal and work life. Get 50% off your plan

it.title: Apache Iceberg 1.12.0 Release
it.summary: The Apache Iceberg community has announced the release of version 1.12.0, featuring significant performance enhancements, expanded write capabilities for Variant and geospatial data types, and new maintenance tasks. Key updates include faster unshredded Variant reads in Spark, multi-engine shredded Variant writes, and Flink-native resolution of equality deletes into row-position deletion vectors. The release also introduces Hilbert-curve clustering for multi-dimensional sorting, expands REST catalog and OpenAPI protocol features, and lays groundwork for Table Format V4.

it.title: ServiceNow Flow Brings a Chat-First Service Desk to Smaller Buyers
it.summary: ServiceNow has introduced Flow, an internal startup product offering a chat-first service desk that operates within Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email. Priced at $2 per conversation and $1 per automation run with a $10,000 annual minimum, Flow allows smaller companies and existing customers to bypass traditional portals and ticket forms. Flow's credit card accessibility and public pricing will open ServiceNow to smaller buyers while challenging third-party chat layers built on top of the platform.

it.title: Hacking the Go compiler to efficiently map IPv4 to IPv6
it.summary: The Go compiler handles mapping IPv4 addresses to IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses inefficiently: the idiomatic netip.AddrFrom16 and As16 pattern runs eight times slower than a native method because of suboptimal compiler optimization. Standard library changes, an unsafe proxy, and custom IR and SSA rewrite rules can eliminate redundant byte-packing and unpacking overhead and achieve native-level performance.

it.title: Amazon explores an $8B Nvidia chip sale-leaseback
it.summary: Amazon is reportedly discussing a financing arrangement that would sell roughly $8 billion of Nvidia chips into a special-purpose vehicle and lease them back for continued use. The proposal highlights how hyperscalers are seeking outside capital to fund AI expansion while investors take on risks tied to hardware depreciation and future compute demand.

it.title: Namespace raises $42M for developer infrastructure
it.summary: Namespace raised a $42 million Series B to expand compute infrastructure for coding agents, builds, and testing across Mac, Windows, and Linux.

it.title: Manage system settings with Endpoint Privilege Management
it.summary: Microsoft has documented an Elevation system settings policy for Endpoint Privilege Management in Intune that allows standard users to modify network settings without local administrator rights.
